not_directly_deployable_note: This file is Noesis governance metadata, not an MCPJungle configuration. MCPJungle's create and update group commands accept only name, description, included_tools, included_servers and excluded_tools. The risk levels, controls, consumers, overlaps and coverage gaps recorded here have no MCPJungle equivalent, so they live in this file and in README.md rather than being invented as configuration keys. mcpjungle_constraints.allowlist_policy: Every generated group uses an explicit included_tools allowlist. No group uses included_servers, so a tool added to a registered server later cannot silently widen a group.
mcpjungle_constraints.empty_group_behaviour: MCPJungle rejects a group whose resolved tool set is empty.
mcpjungle_constraints.unknown_tool_behaviour: MCPJungle rejects creation when a listed tool does not exist or is disabled.
mcpjungle_constraints.disabled_tool_behaviour: A tool disabled globally is removed from every group endpoint. A group that lists it still shows it in its stored definition, but it is no longer callable.

unsupported_requested_categories.reason: No DevOps or infrastructure server is registered in this gateway. There is no Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, Ansible, CI or cloud-provider tool among the 308 discovered tools. The nearest surfaces are n8n workflow inspection (workflow-inspection) and deployment and usage status (observability); neither is a DevOps tool surface, and naming either 'devops-readonly' would misrepresent it. Infrastructure execution lives in the noesis-ansible repository and in the Hermes terminal toolset, not in MCPJungle.

No network-device or network-automation server is registered in this gateway. The UniFi MCP server is a separate, directly configured Hermes connection (unifi-local) that does not traverse MCPJungle, so it cannot be expressed as an MCPJungle group. That also means the UniFi surface is governed by Hermes connection configuration, not by any group in this catalog.
No cloud-provider server (AWS, GCP, Azure, Cloudflare) is registered in this gateway.

Same as cloud-infrastructure-readonly: no cloud-provider server is registered. The closest mutation surface is Mintlify deployment administration (platform-administration), which manages one documentation site and is not cloud infrastructure.
No blockchain, wallet, miner or DePIN data server is registered. The noesis-ledger domain can only be served by the generic web-research, academic-research and market-research groups.

No spending, transfer, trading, payment or wallet tool exists anywhere in the 308-tool inventory. Every financial capability present is read-only research, grouped under market-research. The one payment-adjacent tool is court-listener__pray_for_document, which sits in legal-alerts under a spending control.

No mail, chat or SMS server is registered in this gateway. The only communications read surface is the Mintlify comment thread, which is what the group of the same name contains. The Herald workflow therefore has no inbox to read from and cannot verify prior outbound correspondence.

n8n data tables and the Mintlify deployment databases provide readable and writable tabular surfaces, and both groups exist. There is no generic SQL database server (no PostgreSQL, MySQL or SQLite tool), so 'database' here means the two tabular stores actually reachable, not a general SQL surface. The one SQL surface present, mintlify__query_analytics, is confined to the docs deployment's own analytics tables and is held in data-analytics.

Deployment status, workflow run history, execution records and provider credit and usage reporting cover the read-only observability surface. There is no metrics, log-aggregation or tracing server (no Prometheus, Grafana or Loki) registered in this gateway, so infrastructure telemetry is not reachable through MCPJungle at all.
n8n provides agent draft authoring, versioning, validation and retirement; the Beacon-managed server provides the memory and trace substrate agents read from. Both groups exist.

Only two genuine security surfaces exist: GitHub secret scanning and Beacon's security findings. There is no SAST, DAST, dependency-audit or container-scanning server registered, so the group cannot cover a full security review.
The GitHub MCP server exposes both surfaces, split across source-control-readonly, source-control-issues-readonly and source-control-write. It is the only source-control server registered.
